title: Proper adic direct image preserves coproducts on the hull
statement:
Fix a universe u, a prime $\ell$, and a field $k$ in universe u of positive
characteristic different from $\ell$. Let $Z,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes
and let $g:Z\to Y$ be a proper $k$-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be
a commutative condensed ring with its specified multiplication and a certificate
of one of the three adic coefficient families [def-sfb-adic-coefficient-certificate].
For $T=Z,Y$, put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$, let $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$
be the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category
[sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], let $\mathcal B_T$ be its bounded constructible
full subcategory [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], and let
$\mathcal L_T=\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal B_T)$ be the full localizing hull, using
ambient coproducts indexed in universe u+1
[def-sfb-bounded-constructible-localizing-closure].
Let $i_Z:\mathcal L_Z\to D_Z$ be the full inclusion and let
$Rg_*:D_Z\to D_Y$ be the actual total right derived module-object pushforward.
For every type I in universe u+1, the functor $Rg_*\circ i_Z$ preserves
I-indexed coproducts. Preservation refers to the canonical comparison induced by
the coprojections, including I empty. No claim is made about arbitrary objects
of $D_Z$.

source.place: Parts (1)-(2): coproduct preservation of the identity-compactification functor.

proof.text: The ordinary module-object categories are Grothendieck abelian. Their derived categories have coproducts of the required universe, and their homology functors preserve these coproducts.

Each lower truncation τ≥a preserves coproducts: the coproduct of objects in D≥a remains in D≥a because homology preserves coproducts. The adjunction universal property of K→τ≥a K therefore constructs an inverse of its canonical coproduct comparison.

Choose c from the proper lower-tail upper-amplitude bound on the source hull. A family A_i in the hull has its ambient coproduct there as well. For any K in the hull and output degree q, apply exact proper pushforward to the triangle τ<q-c K → K → τ≥q-c K. The first term after pushforward has upper amplitude q-1. Its cohomology in q and q+1 vanishes, so the long exact sequence makes H^q of K→τ≥q-c K invertible.

The truncated family has common lower bound q-c, so qcqs bounded-below coproduct continuity applies. The square of canonical coproduct comparisons and truncation maps commutes by naturality. Its two vertical maps and its truncated comparison are invertible after H^q; therefore so is the original comparison after H^q. Factor out the homology coproduct comparison and use detection of derived isomorphisms by every H^q.

Thus pushforward preserves the ambient coproduct of every family from the source hull. The hull inclusion preserves those coproducts by its definition, giving the stated preservation for the composite. Discrete diagram isomorphisms identify the chosen family diagrams with arbitrary diagrams of that shape; all steps also cover the empty family.

proof_origin.place: Parts (1)-(2), reduced to one uniform lower-truncation input on the hull and the proved bounded-below qcqs coproduct theorem. The Lean proof uses no equality Dctf=Dbc and no separate ind-heart interface.
